answer: Reputation-decay identity pricing. Each new agent identity starts with a low trust score that decays like a yarrow stalk in a gale—slowly at first, then sharply. High-value actions (payments, contracts) require a minimum score, so an attacker must sustain each fake identity through real, costly interactions for weeks before it can act. The timber of the cost curve: maintaining N identities in parallel scales linearly with N, while benefits per identity stay fixed, making duplication unprofitable past a small threshold.
